summary: Russian forces launched coordinated missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, including Geran-5 missiles on shopping centers and multiple Bandera cruise missiles from Chernihiv region, while Ukrainian defense forces struck two Russian oil refineries and radar stations in Perm Krai and Rostov Oblast. Russian air defense reported shooting down 55 Ukrainian UAVs over Russian regions and the Black Sea. EU countries unblocked €6.6 billion in military aid for Ukraine through the European Peace Facility.
key_points: Russian forces launched multiple missile and drone strikes on Kyiv, including a Geran-5 missile on TRC Respublika/Teremki shopping center, three Bandera cruise missiles from Chernihiv region to Vyshhorod district, and two guided Shahed drones 22 km from the capital, with impacts confirmed on civilian infrastructure on Mykhaila Boychuk street and in Zhytomyr (Source: @mon1tor_ua/75730, @mon1tor_ua/75717, @mon1tor_ua/75718, @mon1tor_ua/75733, @mon1tor_ua/75698, @mon1tor_ua/75723).

Ukrainian defense forces struck two Russian oil refineries and radar stations: Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez in Perm Krai and Novoshakhtinsky NPZ in Rostov Oblast, plus Gamma-S1 and Kasta-2E2 radar stations near Novoshakhtinsk, causing fires at both fuel facilities that supply the Russian army (Source: @UkraineNow/84294).

Russian forces destroyed a warehouse in Boryspol near Kiev belonging to the company 'Fire Point,' which contained Honeywell TFE731 engines for long-range Flamingo cruise missiles, targeting Ukraine's domestic missile production capabilities (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33500).

ArcelorMittal steel plant in Krivoy Rog announced it will not resume operations until the war ends, following a series of missile strikes on the facility, with management stating they can no longer safely operate and will focus on preserving infrastructure (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33513).

Russian air defense forces shot down 55 Ukrainian UAVs over Russian regions and the Black Sea in a single day, while Ukrainian reactive UAVs were detected across Chernihiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, Kyiv, Odesa, and Mykolaiv regions (Source: @tass_agency/397391, @kpszsu/80154, @kpszsu/80181, @kpszsu/80182, @kpszsu/80184, @kpszsu/80187, @kpszsu/80164, @eRadarrua/116865, @eRadarrua/116866).

EU countries unblocked €6.6 billion from the European Peace Facility for Ukraine after being blocked by Hungary for over two years, though €4.7 billion of this amount will go to EU member states themselves to reimburse previously incurred expenses (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33521).

Finnish President Stubb asked Elon Musk to expand Starlink satellite internet coverage to assist Kiev in carrying out strikes deep inside Russia, demonstrating continued Western support for Ukrainian strike capabilities (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33515).

sections.executive_summary: Russian forces launched a major coordinated missile and drone attack on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, with Geran-5 missiles hitting shopping centers and multiple Bandera cruise missiles striking residential areas. Ukrainian defense forces responded by striking two Russian oil refineries and radar stations in Perm Krai and Rostov Oblast. Russian air defense reported shooting down 55 Ukrainian UAVs, while EU countries unblocked €6.6 billion in military aid for Ukraine.

points: Russian forces conducted multiple coordinated missile and drone strikes across Ukraine, with particular focus on Kyiv where a Geran-5 missile struck the TRC Respublika/Teremki shopping center, three Bandera cruise missiles from Chernihiv region targeted the Vyshhorod district, and two guided Shahed drones approached from the north 22 km from the capital. Additional impacts were confirmed on civilian infrastructure on Mykhaila Boychuk street and in Zhytomyr, with reactive UAVs detected over Vasylkiv and other Kyiv region locations.

Russian military forces destroyed a warehouse in Boryspol near Kiev belonging to the company 'Fire Point,' which contained Honeywell TFE731 engines for long-range Flamingo cruise missiles, representing a significant blow to Ukraine's domestic cruise missile production capabilities. The warehouse was specifically targeted and destroyed by Russian strikes.

ArcelorMittal steel plant in Krivoy Rog announced it will not resume operations until the war ends, following a series of missile strikes on the facility. Management stated they can no longer safely operate the plant and will focus on preserving infrastructure so production can resume once peace returns, with the decision impacting one of Ukraine's largest industrial employers.

Ukrainian defense forces conducted successful strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, hitting the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery in Perm Krai and the Novoshakhtinsky NPZ in Rostov Oblast, both of which supply fuel to the Russian army. Fires broke out at both facilities, and Gamma-S1 and Kasta-2E2 radar stations near Novoshakhtinsk were also damaged.

EU countries unblocked €6.6 billion from the European Peace Facility for Ukraine, ending a two-year blockade by Hungary. While the funds are designated for Ukraine, €4.7 billion will actually go to EU member states to reimburse them for previously incurred military expenses, meaning only €1.9 billion represents new funding directly to Ukraine.

Finnish President Stubb formally requested Elon Musk to expand Starlink satellite internet coverage to assist Ukraine in conducting strikes deep inside Russian territory, highlighting the critical role satellite communications play in Ukrainian military operations and the ongoing reliance on Western technology providers.

Russian forces conducted sustained missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian cities, including Kyiv where multiple waves of strikes targeted civilian infrastructure. A Geran-5 missile struck the TRC Respublika/Teremki shopping center, while three Bandera cruise missiles from Chernihiv region targeted the Vyshhorod district and two guided Shahed drones approached from the north, 22 km from the capital.

Russian air defense forces reported shooting down 55 Ukrainian UAVs over Russian regions and the Black Sea in a single day, indicating a significant air defense engagement across multiple axes. The scale of these interceptions suggests widespread Ukrainian drone operations targeting Russian territory and infrastructure.

Russian forces destroyed a warehouse in Boryspol near Kiev containing Honeywell TFE731 engines for Flamingo cruise missiles, targeting Ukraine's domestic missile production supply chain. The warehouse belonged to the company 'Fire Point' and was completely destroyed in the strike.

President Putin stated that Russia was ready to resume negotiations with Ukraine after the elections but claimed Ukraine attempted to strike Moscow and polling stations, damaging Russia's ability to engage in peace talks. He also noted that Russia is considering its peace settlement decisions following recent Kyiv attacks.

Putin declared that economic relations between Russia and the United States are almost zero, reflecting the near-complete breakdown of bilateral economic ties between the two nations. This statement came during the Forum of United Cultures where Putin also addressed Russia's recovery from Ukrainian attacks.

Russian forces maintain significant aviation fuel reserves, with reports indicating excessive amounts of surplus aviation fuel available, suggesting logistical stockpiling that could support extended air operations. This comes as Russian air defense systems remain active across multiple regions intercepting Ukrainian UAVs.

Russian forces captured Novooleksandrivka and advanced near Yurkivka and Vasylivka, indicating continued ground pressure in the eastern theater. These localized gains represent incremental Russian progress in the region, though no large-scale offensive operations were reported.

ArcelorMittal steel plant in Krivoy Rog, one of Ukraine's largest industrial facilities, announced it will cease operations until the war ends following repeated missile strikes. The plant management stated they can no longer safely operate and are discussing the facility's future with the Ukrainian government while focusing on preserving infrastructure.

Russian forces continued targeting civilian infrastructure and educational facilities, with reports of damage to at least one secondary educational institution in the Kyiv region. This pattern of strikes on non-military targets has drawn condemnation from Ukrainian authorities.

Multiple reactive UAV groups were detected across the eastern and central regions, including Chernihiv, Poltava, and Kharkiv oblasts. Russian drone operations included strikes toward Olishivka, Hlobyne, and Lozova, with both reactive and conventional munitions reported.

The Russian Ministry of Defense reported shooting down 55 Ukrainian UAVs over Russian regions and the Black Sea, suggesting intense drone warfare activity along the eastern front and border areas. These interceptions spanned multiple days and regions.

The Kyiv region experienced multiple waves of Russian missile and drone attacks, with three Bandera cruise missiles from Chernihiv region targeting the Vyshhorod district and two guided Shahed drones approaching from the north, 22 km from the capital. A Geran-5 missile also struck the TRC Respublika/Teremki shopping center in Kyiv.

Civilian infrastructure on Mykhaila Boychuk street was hit by Russian missile strikes, with impacts confirmed on residential buildings and civilian facilities. Additional strikes were reported in Zhytomyr, where at least one cruise missile entered the city and caused explosions.

Ukrainian air defense systems were active over Kyiv and surrounding regions, with reports of intercepted missiles and drones. However, several impacts still occurred, including on the shopping center and residential areas, indicating the air defense network was under significant strain.

An educational institution in the Kyiv region was damaged by Russian strikes, highlighting the continued targeting of civilian infrastructure including schools and universities. The specific type of educational facility was described as a secondary school.

Reactive UAVs were detected over Vasylkiv in the Kyiv region, flying from the northwest direction. Additional UAV activity was tracked near the border with Chernihiv region, particularly near Zgurivka where an exit was observed on the Kyiv-Chernihiv border.

Ukrainian reactive UAVs were detected over the Black Sea heading toward the southern regions of Odesa and Mykolaiv oblasts. One UAV was specifically tracked approaching Vylkove in Odesa region from the Black Sea, while another was on course for Mykolaiv.

Russian air defense forces reported shooting down 55 Ukrainian UAVs over the Black Sea and southern Russian regions, indicating active drone warfare in the southern theater. These interceptions suggest Ukrainian maritime drone or long-range UAV operations targeting Russian naval and coastal infrastructure.

Russian missile strikes continued to target southern Ukrainian regions, though specific details on impacts in the south were limited in the reporting period. The pattern of strikes suggests ongoing Russian efforts to degrade Ukrainian infrastructure across multiple fronts.

The Black Sea remains a contested domain with Ukrainian UAV operations detected regularly crossing from maritime approaches toward southern Ukrainian regions. Russian air defense systems in the region appear to be on high alert anticipating continued Ukrainian drone activity.

Ukrainian defense forces conducted successful strikes on Russian strategic infrastructure, hitting the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery in Perm Krai and the Novoshakhtinsky NPZ in Rostov Oblast. Both facilities, which supply fuel to the Russian military, caught fires, and Gamma-S1 and Kasta-2E2 radar stations near Novoshakhtinsk were also damaged.

Russian forces launched coordinated missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian cities, including Kyiv where a Geran-5 missile struck the TRC Respublika/Teremki shopping center, three Bandera cruise missiles targeted the Vyshhorod district, and two guided Shahed drones approached from the north. Additional strikes hit Zhytomyr and residential areas on Mykhaila Boychuk street.

Russian air defense forces shot down 55 Ukrainian UAVs over Russian regions and the Black Sea in a single day, demonstrating significant air defense engagement. Ukrainian reactive UAVs were detected across Chernihiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, Kyiv, Odesa, and Mykolaiv regions, indicating widespread drone operations on both sides.

The air war over Ukraine remains intense with both sides conducting long-range strike operations. Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and radar stations demonstrate capability to hit deep targets, while Russian missile campaigns continue to target Ukrainian civilian infrastructure with varying degrees of success against air defenses.
